observation_summary: The CMAESOptimizer fails when provided with bounds that cause overflow during normalization, leading to NaN parameters being passed to the fitness function. The test expects a NumberIsTooLargeException but receives a MathIllegalStateException.
reasoning_summary: The fix introduces a new validation check (a loop with an if-condition) to detect when the difference between upper and lower bounds results in infinity (overflow). This check explicitly throws a NumberIsTooLargeException when the condition is met, preventing the subsequent invalid computation. This is a classic missing guard/validation check.
evidence_used: The fix adds a loop that checks if (Double.isInfinite(boundaries[1][i] - boundaries[0][i]))
The fix throws a NumberIsTooLargeException when the condition is met
The bug report states that large bounds cause NaN parameters due to overflow during normalization
The failing test expects a NumberIsTooLargeException

alternative_types.why_not_primary: The fix does not change the normalization algorithm itself, but rather adds a guard to prevent the algorithm from executing with invalid inputs.
